text:
anya (pm): Quick sync — we need to lock the prioritization and rollout approach for the 'Scoped Responses' customer ask. They asked for a toggle + safer canary path. Can we RICE this and agree launch criteria + fallback plan today?

matt (eng): I can do a first-pass RICE. We should also decide if this is feature-first or experiment-first. Feature-first -> faster for customer but more cost. Experiment-first -> less work but slower.

jun (data): I ran an early analysis of impacted requests: ~3% of prod queries would hit the new routing logic if enabled globally. If we target 1% initial traffic that's ~33k requests/day.

anya (pm): Proposed RICE inputs: Reach = 3 (3% of requests => medium), Impact = 6 (reduces misrouted responses for enterprise customers), Confidence = 5, Effort = 4 (backend + toggle + tests). RICE = (3*6*5)/4 = 22.5 -> round 23. Thoughts?

matt (eng): Fine baseline. My concern: effort underestimates QA + rollout safety. If we add automatic fallback instrumentation it's +1 effort. That drops RICE to (3*6*5)/5 = 18.

carla (sales): From the customer side, they'd accept a phased delivery if we guarantee a hard kill switch and audit logs. They want the toggle visible in console and an SLA note. Prioritize visibility.

sam (design): We'll need a compact toggle UI, default off for new orgs, and clear tooltip about latency/cost tradeoffs. I can mock a minimal UI in 2 days.

ellie (qa): QA checklist: unit + e2e for routing logic, canary metrics (error-rate, wrong-model-routes), chaos test for partial KV cache loss. Estimate QA effort 1.5 dev-weeks.

olivia (sre): Rollout plan proposal: internal-only smoke -> 0.5% external (alpha orgs) -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%. At each step evaluate: p95 latency delta, error rate, downstream token cost delta. Auto-rollback threshold: any step with error-rate increase > 0.5pp or latency p95 increase > 20%.

anya (pm): That sequencing looks good. Can we make the canary policy symmetric so it supports both 'traffic-split' and 'model-variant fallback'?

matt (eng): Yes. We can implement a routing policy with prioritized fallbacks. High-level policy (pseudo JSON):

```json
{
  "policy": "staged",
  "steps": [
    {"pct": 0.5, "criteria": {"max_error_pp": 0.5, "max_p95_increase_pct": 20}},
    {"pct": 1, "criteria": {"max_error_pp": 0.5, "max_p95_increase_pct": 15}},
    {"pct": 5, "criteria": {"max_error_pp": 0.4, "max_p95_increase_pct": 10}},
    {"pct": 25, "criteria": {"max_error_pp": 0.25, "max_p95_increase_pct": 7}},
    {"pct": 100, "criteria": {"max_error_pp": 0.1, "max_p95_increase_pct": 5}}
  ],
  "fallbacks": ["model_variant","region_fallback","hard_kill"]
}
```

jun (data): For metrics, we'll surface: request_count, wrong_route_rate, p95_latency, token_cost_per_1k, and customer_quality_score (synthetic eval). I'll attach a dashboard once devs wire metrics.

olivia (sre): Add one more safeguard: a rolling rollback that targets affected nodes rather than global kill so we don't cascade. Also require a manual approval for >25% step unless exec opt-in.

matt (eng): Implementation questions: do we treat this as a long-lived feature flag in our existing flags service or a deploy-time routing config? Flags = faster, routing config = safer for audits. Need direction.

anya (pm): Given customer requirement for visible control in console and audit logs, prefer routing config surfaced in console but backed by a flag for rapid kill. So both: routing config for staged controls + emergency flag.

carla (sales): Important: customer expects data residency to be respected. If we route to variant in different region, the customer will push back. Make region fallback opt-in per org.

sam (design): UI note — if region fallback is off, show an explicit warning on enable.

ellie (qa): Can we add a synthetic prompt set for regression detection? Put a simple threshold: quality-drop > 3% triggers rollback. Jun?

jun (data): I can craft a 100-prompt regression set representative of their workload. We'll compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish quality proxy and a normalized quality score. 3% seems reasonable.

matt (eng): Dev timeline: trunk changes + toggle + metrics wiring = 2 sprints, plus 1 sprint for canary infra & console surface. Total ~3 sprints. If we need to accelerate, we can reduce scope by launching without console toggle (flag only) and then ship console later. That increases risk for customers.

anya (pm): Tradeoff decision needed: ship in 3 sprints with console vs ship flag-only in 2 sprints. Vote please.

carla (sales): I'll take flag-only if we get explicit SLA language and a rollout date to share. Customer will accept temporary flag-only for faster delivery. :+1:

olivia (sre): Prefer full console from ops safety POV but flag-only + documented kill switch is acceptable short-term. :thumbsup:

ellie (qa): Flag-only shortens QA scope slightly, OK with mitigation tests.

matt (eng): I'll scope for flag-only green path as a fast follow in sprint 1, then console in sprint 2.

anya (pm): Consensus: do flag-first (2 sprints) with strict canary policy + dashboards + auto-rollback, then add console + org-level controls in follow-up. Action items: matt -> final RICE update and PRD edits; jun -> regression prompt set + dashboard skeleton; olivia -> rollout runbook + runbook rehearsals; sam -> minimal toggle UX for sprint 2; carla -> notify customer of phased plan and SLA note; ellie -> QA plan.

deploy-bot: New deploy window scheduled: 2026-11-08 03:00 UTC for internal smoke (not customer-facing).

anya (pm): Thanks all — I'll update the PRD with final numbers and scope. If anyone has objections to the rollback thresholds above speak now, otherwise I'll mark as agreed and move to planning. :white_check_mark:
